How often do World Bank projects cite forced-displacement data?

Evidence from 2,261 projects, read through 4,679 Project Appraisal and Project Information Documents

Count by
Out of

Of 2,052 projects that use data (233 of 2,052, 11%), the passages read tie data to forced displacement. How reliable is this?

  1. 2,261projects reviewed: every one with a PAD or PID in the collection
  2. 2,052use data in the passages read
  3. 233tie data to forced displacement

Forced-displacement data appears in every region and concentrates in fragile settings

By approval year the share runs from 8% (2026) to 14% (2022).

Among the 114 countries with at least 5 projects, the share runs from 0% (Uzbekistan) to 57% (South Sudan).

So whatForced-displacement data is cited where displacement is concentrated, and rarely elsewhere. A project with no detected mention is not proof of no displacement work: only sampled passages were read.

Which sources the related mentions name

3% of the 23,292 candidate mentions in this view relate to forced displacement. Three families sit above that rate: UNHCR and displacement systems 96% (29x), Conflict and violence monitoring 82% (25x), Humanitarian reports and assessments 13% (4x). The rest sit at or below it: Other named source (14,391 mentions) at 2% and Surveys and household studies (4,739 mentions) at 3%.

The families are rule-based groups of the mention text, so the two named for displacement sort out by definition; the rest sit near the corpus rate and say little about the sources themselves.

Which sources the related mentions name

3% of the 24,103 candidate mentions in this view relate to forced displacement. Three families sit above that rate: UNHCR and displacement systems 96% (29x), Conflict and violence monitoring 82% (25x), Humanitarian reports and assessments 13% (4x). The rest sit at or below it: Other named source (14,865 mentions) at 2% and Surveys and household studies (4,873 mentions) at 3%.

The families are rule-based groups of the mention text, so the two named for displacement sort out by definition; the rest sit near the corpus rate and say little about the sources themselves.

Passages behind the labels

Every related mention in this view, with the sentence it came from. The label, the detector that fired and the theme score are printed with each passage.

Frequently asked questions

What period does this sample cover?

Approval dates in this sample run from 2020 to 2026. The collection holds 2,261 projects with a confirmed PAD or PID; 2,261 of them have at least one reviewed passage and enter this analysis.

Out of which projects?

Those that use data (the default) counts projects with at least one data mention judged used. All reviewed adds the 209 projects that mention data only as plans, bare figures or sources not relied on. Unreviewed projects are never a denominator: their use is unknown, not absent. The number beside each button is the size of that denominator in the view shown.

Projects or documents?

A project usually has more than one PAD or PID. Projects count a project once: it is related if any of its reviewed passages is. Documents count each PAD or PID on its own. The project view is the reporting unit, because region, sector and approval year belong to the project. A project has more text in which a mention can appear, so its share is higher. The same document sometimes arrives from two collections under two ids; it is counted once, by its World Bank document id, and a passage read twice counts once. 4,708 confirmed document ids are 4,679 distinct documents.

What counts as forced-displacement-related data?

A source the passage ties to displacement: refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced people, return or resettlement, or a figure on those populations. A source UNHCR produces counts. A topic such as agriculture or health does not count on its own, and neither does a fragile or conflict-affected country, a section heading, or a nearby sentence about conflict.

The label is the explicit-source-link-v2 relation rubric, which requires that explicit link.

What counts as using data?

Each data mention was judged for use: does the passage rely on existing data, or only name it, plan to collect it, or cite a bare figure? Only mentions judged as used count.

Why not count datasets?

The same source is named many ways (“UNHCR”, “UNHCR Registration”, “proGres v.4 registration database”), so counts of distinct datasets are unreliable. Whether a project or document is related is a clear yes or no. Source names are grouped by rule from the mention text for display only.

How reliable are these figures?

Every number is counted from the records; none is typed in. The figures rest on AI-extracted data-use mentions from a sample of passages: a model found each data mention, a separate pass judged whether the data was used, and the label was written against a written rubric, quoting the passage words behind it.

Every share is a floor. Each project was judged from a few sampled passages, not its full documents. A passage is an excerpt of a PAD or PID, about a page long, taken where the text mentions data; it is not a data mention, and one passage can hold several. 95 of the 2,052 data-using projects have only one passage read. The more we read, the more we find: of the data-using projects with one passage read, 2% are related; with five or more, 14% are. Read in full, more projects would likely count.

Reading more text would likely find more: the share rises from 2% among projects with one passage read to 14% among those with five or more.

Coverage and limits

2,261 projects had passages reviewed, through 4,679 of their 4,708 confirmed PADs and PIDs. All 2,052 data-using projects were approved in 2020 or later, so this describes recent practice and does not show a trend. Sector, region and approval year come from the World Bank Projects API. Countries with fewer than 5 units and approval years with fewer than 15 are left out of the map and the trend. Review sets used: umar_pads, umar_pads_500. A PAD/PID counts only when the World Bank documents catalogue confirms it: the document exists, has the stated type and belongs to the stated project. The same document arriving from two collections is counted once, by its World Bank document id.

Every figure comes from the records in rafmacalaba/pad-pid-displacement on Hugging Face, snapshot 845510cb3644 (Jev 1.13 theme scores and explicit-source-link-v2 relation labels). Labels from the explicit-source-link-v2 relation rubric.
